items.claim: 1:1-1:7 is one exposition movement: the regnal dateline of 1:1 opens it, and it closes at 1:7 because 1:8 begins with Daniel as a new acting subject and a new initiative. The siege and vessels (1:1-1:2), the order to the chief official (1:3-1:5) and the naming of the four (1:6-1:7) share one function, setting the stage; narrative fits the closed vocabulary and medium fits an unmarked chapter.
items.both_sides: Seam 1:7/1:8. Close side: 1:7 ends the list of new names, the last item of the setting. Onset side: 1:8 names Daniel as subject of a resolve, the first act of any youth. No paragraph mark stands anywhere in 1:1-1:20 (WLC only), so the seam rests on the text.
evidence: MEASURED (my script over the device inventory): dateline entry at MT 1:1, numeral three, reign Jehoiakim; and_he_said at 1:3; vayehi at 1:6; mareh at 1:4.
MEASURED (my script over the mark layer, WLC only): no PE or SAMEKH after any verse of 1:1-1:20; ketiv/qere note at 1:4 and at no other verse of 1:1-1:7; no paseq in the span.

MEASURED (my script over the Hebrew witness): the verb 'give' as a separate word with God or the Lord as giver stands in chapter 1 at 1:2, 1:9 and 1:17 only, one in each of the first three rows; this is support from the text for a three-movement reading of 1:1-1:20 (the reading is INFERRED).

Rejected alternative weighed: a cut at 1:2/1:3 is a real rival (change of place and of action) and the row's answer, that the king of 1:3 is unnamed and depends on 1:1-1:2, holds in WEB 1:3 'The king spoke to Ashpenaz'. The other rival, 1:5/1:6 at the vayehi clause, is answered in device_notes.

Low note, not a challenge: the inventory also records a year word and a day word at 1:5 (the three-year term, not a date); the row does not disclose them. The three-year term of 1:5 is what 1:18 resumes.
Hebrew tag checked: the tag string is an exact substring of the witness line Dan.1.1.

items.claim: 1:8-1:16 is one test episode with resolve, request, objection, proposal, trial and outcome; it closes at 1:16, where the Hebrew uses a durative construction (vayehi plus two participles) for the steward's continuing practice, a summary close, and 1:17 then fronts a new subject.
items.both_sides: Seam 1:16/1:17. Close side: 1:16 states a lasting state of affairs after the test, with the same actors and no new subject. Onset side: 1:17 opens with the fronted noun phrase for the four youths and turns from food to God's gift of learning. Seam 1:7/1:8 is weighed under the first row.
evidence: EXTRACTED (Hebrew witness, Dan.1.16): the verse opens with vayehi and has two participles, 'taking away' and 'giving'; WEB 1:16 has the simple past 'took away' and 'gave'. The row's 'keeps giving' is a fair reading of the participles and INFERRED is not too strong.

EXTRACTED (WEB 1:10): the chief official is the speaker of 'I fear my lord the king'. The row's phrase for his fear reads in its list as the fear he voices; a second parse (a fear felt toward him) is grammatically possible but is not the natural one, and I do not rate it a defect.
MEASURED (my script over the device inventory): and_he_said at 1:10 and 1:11; day words at 1:12, 1:14, 1:15; vayehi at 1:16; mareh at 1:13: all as the row lists them.
MEASURED (my script over the mark layer, WLC only): no mark, no ketiv/qere note and no paseq in 1:8-1:16, so 'unmarked stretch' is true and nothing is undisclosed.
EXTRACTED (WEB): 'ten days' stands in 1:12, 1:14 and 1:15.

Rejected alternative weighed: closing at 1:15 so that the vayehi of 1:16 opens a unit is the strongest rival, because vayehi is the only formal signal in the area; the row's answer (1:16 brings no new subject and reports the result) is sound, and vayehi at 1:6 and 1:21 likewise does not open a movement by itself.
Hebrew tag checked: exact substring of Dan.1.8.

items.claim: 1:17-1:20 is the sequel and outcome: a fronted subject at 1:17 with God's gift, then the presentation at the appointed end (1:18) and the examination result (1:19-1:20). It stops before 1:21, which leaves the scene for a notice of Daniel's tenure.
items.both_sides: Seam 1:20/1:21. Close side: 1:20 ends the examination with its superlative verdict, the last narrated event of the scene. Onset side: 1:21 has vayehi with Daniel alone as subject and a time span that runs decades past the scene. Seam 1:16/1:17 is weighed under the second row.
evidence: EXTRACTED (WEB 1:17, 1:18): 'Now as for these four youths, God gave them' and 'At the end of the days which the king had appointed'.
MEASURED (my script over the device inventory): hazon at 1:17; day word at 1:18; 1:21 is listed as a year word that is not a dateline and is the first end-review item (regnal terminus).
MEASURED (my script over the mark layer, WLC only): PE after 1:21; no mark in 1:17-1:20; no ketiv/qere note in the span.

Rival weighed: 1:17 could be read as the close of the test (the gift as its result) with 1:18-1:20 alone as the examination. The fronted subject of 1:17 and the return of 'visions and dreams' in the king's inquiry favour the row; the 1:18 interval clause is texture and does not open a unit alone.
Hebrew tag checked: exact substring of Dan.1.17.

items.claim: 1:21 is a one-verse closing notice: it names an end point of Daniel's tenure (the first year of Cyrus) and narrates no event of the scene. summary_notice is the right type, a one-verse row is allowed for it, and it is not joined forward to the dateline of 2:1.
items.both_sides: Seam 1:21/2:1 (parent seam). Close side: the tenure notice, with a PE after 1:21 (WLC only). Onset side: the regnal dateline of 2:1, a new reign year and a new plot. Seam 1:20/1:21 is weighed under the third row.
evidence: EXTRACTED (WEB 1:21): 'Daniel continued even to the first year of King Cyrus.'

MEASURED (my script over the device inventory): vayehi at 1:21; 1:21 is outside the eight datelines and inside the year-word-not-a-dateline list; the first end-review item asks whether a regnal year named as an end point is a dateline. The row's pointer to that item is true to the file.
MEASURED (my script over the mark layer, WLC only): PE after 1:21; dateline entry at MT 2:1.
Confidence: medium is not rounded up; both sides of both seams have text evidence. That the verse 'frames the whole court story' is a reading, and the row tiers it INFERRED.
Hebrew tag checked: exact substring of Dan.1.21.

items.claim: 2:1-2:4 holds the dateline, the dream, the summons and the first round of the exchange (the king's statement at 2:3, the Chaldeans' reply at 2:4). The cut after 2:4 falls between rounds, not inside one: each of the three rounds is a royal speech plus a reply (2:3 and 2:4; 2:5-2:6 and 2:7; 2:8-2:9 and 2:10-2:11). The edge is weak and medium_low is the honest grade.
items.both_sides: Seam 2:4/2:5. Close side: 2:4 completes the first request-and-reply pair. Onset side: 2:5 opens only with the answering formula, a weak connective, and the king's speech answers 2:4, so the dialogue runs on; what is new at 2:5 is the threat and promise. No mark follows 2:4 (WLC only). The evidence is real on the close side and thin on the onset side, which is what medium_low says.
evidence: MEASURED (my script over the language-zone file): 2:1-2:3 are H, 2:4 is mixed with 12 words and the change before word 5; the row's language field 'mixed' and its statement of the switch agree with the file, and it places no boundary inside the verse.
MEASURED (my script over the Hebrew and Aramaic witness): the row's Aramaic quotation is an exact substring of Dan.2.4 and is words 5 to 7 of its 12 words, in the Aramaic half as the row says.

MEASURED (my script over the device inventory and mark layer): dateline entry at MT 2:1 (second year, Nebuchadnezzar); and_he_said at 2:2 and 2:3; the court greeting formula at 2:4; ketiv/qere note at 2:4; PE after 1:21; no mark in 2:1-2:12.
EXTRACTED (WEB 2:7): 'They answered the second time', the text's own count of the replies, which makes 2:4 the first.

Rejected alternative weighed: a cut at 2:3/2:4 is the strongest rival and would split the first round and make the language switch look like a seam. A cut at 2:2/2:3 (setting against speech) is the other candidate; it would leave a dialogue row of eleven verses, over the size limit, on a weak speech verb.

Low note: the rationale's ground for the close ('2:5 is the king's answer to that reply') names what binds 2:5 to 2:4; the ground that separates them is the round structure, which the rejected-alternative field does state.
Hebrew tags checked: both tag strings are exact substrings of Dan.2.1 and Dan.2.4.

items.claim: The span 2:5-2:13 is a sound unit (rounds two and three of the exchange and their outcome, the death decree), but its onset edge is the same 2:4/2:5 edge that the row before it grades medium_low and calls weak. This row grades medium and does not weigh that edge at all. One edge cannot carry two grades.
items.both_sides: No cut is proposed. Seam 2:4/2:5 (onset): thin on the onset side, since 2:5 opens with the answering formula only and continues the dialogue. Seam 2:13/2:14 (close): strong from both sides. 2:12-2:13 give the outcome and the decree goes out; 2:14 brings Daniel in as actor; a PE follows 2:13 (WLC only).

suggested_fix.fact: The onset of this row at 2:5 rests on a dialogue turn alone: the king's speech answers the reply of 2:4 and opens with a weak answering formula, and no mark follows 2:4. The grade should say so, as the grade of the row before it does.

evidence: EXTRACTED (rows file): the preceding row, on the same edge, has confidence medium_low and says the edge at 2:4 is expected to stay weak; this row has confidence medium and its rationale speaks only of the close.

MEASURED (my script over the device inventory): the strict answering formula stands at 2:5, 2:7 and 2:8; 2:10 is in the loose list only. Second finding, low: the row lists all four verses under one unqualified formula name, where the inventory keeps two lists. The fact to install is that 2:10 is a loose-form hit.

MEASURED (my script over the mark layer, WLC only): PE after 2:13; no other mark in 2:5-2:13; ketiv/qere notes in the span at 2:5, 2:9 and 2:10 and at no other verse, so the row's list is complete and exact; one other note, at 2:9; no paseq.
MEASURED (my script over the language-zone file): all nine verses 2:5-2:13 are A. The row's language sentence carries no genre word.

EXTRACTED (WEB 2:13): 'They sought Daniel and his companions to be slain.' The last clause of the close already points to the next row's actor; it does not weaken the seam, since the search is part of the decree's execution.
Rejected alternative weighed: closing at 2:11 is a fair rival and rightly refused (2:12 opens with a weak connective and reports the result of the failed exchange).
Hebrew tag checked: exact substring of Dan.2.13.

items.claim: The cut at 2:16/2:17 is right, but the rationale gives the paragraph mark as the reason the movement ends ('ends at the PE after 2:16'). A mark informs and does not decide. The text grounds exist and sit only in the rejected-alternative field: 2:16 ends Daniel's steps at court with his request to the king, and 2:17 moves him to his house and to new hearers.
items.both_sides: No cut is proposed. Seam 2:16/2:17: close side, 2:16 is the last of three court steps (reply to Arioch, question, audience) and ends on the request for time; onset side, 2:17 keeps Daniel as subject and opens with a weak 'then', but changes place (his house) and hearers (the three companions), and turns from court business to prayer. A PE follows 2:16 (WLC only). Seam 2:13/2:14: close side, the decree goes out; onset side, Daniel acts for the first time in the tale; a PE follows 2:13.

suggested_fix.fact: The close of this row rests on the text: the audience with the king at 2:16 ends the court steps, and 2:17 changes place and hearers. The PE after 2:16 is single-witness information beside that, not the ground.

evidence: EXTRACTED (rows file): the rationale's only ground for the close is the mark; the change of place appears in the rejected-alternative field.
EXTRACTED (WEB 2:16, 2:17): 'Daniel went in, and desired of the king that he would appoint him a time'; 'Then Daniel went to his house'.
MEASURED (my script over the mark layer, WLC only): PE after 2:13 and after 2:16; no ketiv/qere note, other note or paseq in 2:14-2:16, so nothing is undisclosed.
MEASURED (my script over the device inventory): 'then' at 2:14 and 2:15 (and at 2:17 and 2:19 in the next row); loose answering formula at 2:15: as the row lists them.

MEASURED (my script over the language-zone file): 2:14-2:16 are A. The row's language sentence ('The span is Aramaic') carries no genre word, so the weakness named for the later rows of this part does not arise here.

Rejected alternative weighed: merging with 2:17-2:19 is the strongest rival (2:16 gets no narrated answer and the same subject runs on); the row's refusal is sound once the text grounds are stated. Medium may stand.
Hebrew tag checked: exact substring of Dan.2.14.

triage_answers.decision: Every tier word in the seven rows was tested against the layer it names and none is stronger than its evidence, and every named layer holds the fact. Two remarks, neither a defect: (1) W1-006 and W1-007 use MEASURED for the language of their span, where the language-zone file calls its own content EXTRACTED; as a range claim over every verse of the span it is true on a scan (all A). (2) W1-002 sets EXTRACTED, device inventory beside a proposal (close at 1:15, vayehi at 1:16 opens); the layer holds only the vayehi hit at 1:16, which is all the tier can cover.
evidence: Opened: the device inventory (datelines entries for MT 1:1 and 2:1; formula lists for vayehi, and_he_said, mareh, hazon, the court greeting, the answering formula strict and loose, because_of_this, then; the year-word and day-word lists; the first end-review item), the mark layer (marks, ketiv/qere, other notes, paseq), the language-zone file (verse_language, mixed_verses), the WEB extract 1:1-2:20 and the Hebrew and Aramaic witness lines 1:2, 1:9, 1:16, 1:17, 1:21, 2:4, 2:5, 2:14, 2:16, 2:17.
W1-001: dateline EXTRACTED device inventory true (entry MT 1:1); ketiv/qere at 1:4 EXTRACTED mark layer true.
W1-002: 'ten days' at 1:12, 1:14, 1:15 EXTRACTED WEB true; unmarked stretch MEASURED mark layer true (no mark in 1:8-1:16); vayehi at 1:16 true.
W1-003: 1:17 and 1:18-1:20 content EXTRACTED WEB true; terminus at 1:21 EXTRACTED device inventory true; PE after 1:21 EXTRACTED mark layer true.
W1-004: end-review item on the terminus EXTRACTED device inventory true; the rest INFERRED and are readings.

W1-005: dateline and content EXTRACTED device inventory and WEB true; switch before word 5 of 12 EXTRACTED language-zone layer true; quotation is words 5-7 of Dan.2.4 and an exact substring; ketiv/qere at 2:4 true.
W1-006: outcome EXTRACTED WEB true; PE after 2:13 true; ketiv/qere list 2:5, 2:9, 2:10 MEASURED true and complete; note at 2:9 true; all A true.
W1-007: content EXTRACTED WEB true; PE after 2:16 true; all A true.

triage_answers.decision: W1-006: the ketiv/qere list (2:5, 2:9, 2:10) equals the mark layer's entries for 2:5-2:13 exactly, none missing and none extra, so MEASURED is true of the range claim. In W1-006 and W1-007 the language sentence carries a language word only ('wholly in the Aramaic section'; 'The span is Aramaic'), with no genre word beside it, so no genre word needs its own tier in these two rows. Notes (a) to (d) concern rows outside this cluster. Context only: the next row (W1-008) does read 'Aramaic narrative' with one MEASURED, which is the form the note describes; it is not my row.
evidence: MEASURED (my script over the mark layer): ketiv/qere keys within 1:1-2:17 are 1:4, 2:4, 2:5, 2:9, 2:10, one note each.
MEASURED (my script over the language-zone file): 2:5-2:16 are twelve A verses.
EXTRACTED (rows file): the device_notes of W1-006 and W1-007.

triage_answers.decision: The clause holds. The Hebrew of 1:16 opens with vayehi and has two participles (taking away, giving), a durative construction; WEB 1:16 has the simple past. 'Keeps giving vegetables' is a reading of the participles and INFERRED is its true tier, not too strong. The verse is rightly the close of the episode.
evidence: EXTRACTED (Hebrew witness, Dan.1.16, read from the line; no morphology layer is among my inputs, so the parsing of the two forms as participles is my reading of the pointed forms).
EXTRACTED (WEB 1:16): 'took away' and 'gave them vegetables'.

triage_answers.decision: The sentence is true and its INFERRED tier is not too strong. At 1:10 the chief official is the speaker and the fear is his own, of the king. In the row's list (request, fear, ten-day proposal) the phrase reads as the fear he voices. A second parse, a fear felt toward him, is grammatically open but not the natural reading; I rate it a residual ambiguity and not a defect. No five-word WEB run stands in the field outside the quotation convention.
evidence: EXTRACTED (WEB 1:10): the chief official says 'I fear my lord the king'.
MEASURED (my script): no five consecutive WEB words from 1:6-1:18 occur in any prose field of W1-002; the same holds for all seven rows against their span and the two verses on each side.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: All thirteen pinned inputs were hashed and matched. The toolkit note and the suite report were hashed but not opened for content; the flag digest was opened only to confirm that no flag is keyed to a W1 row.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: My findings rest on the rows, the strategy, the device inventory, the mark layer, the language-zone file and the two witnesses, not on the suite's own checks.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The grade of W1-006 depends on whether a row's confidence must reflect its weaker edge. I read the grading rule that way because the row before it is graded on the same edge.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: If a row's grade is meant to describe its span as a whole, medium may stand for W1-006 and the fix would be a sentence weighing the onset edge instead.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The parsing of the two forms in 1:16 as participles, and the count of the verb 'give' in chapter 1, come from the pointed text and a consonantal word match; no morphology layer is among my inputs.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: The durative reading of 1:16 and the three-movement support for the rows of chapter 1 are INFERRED from the bytes, not EXTRACTED from a parsed layer.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether 1:17 belongs with 1:18-1:20 or closes the test episode is a class of question (a narrator's summary at a hinge) on which form evidence points one way but not strongly.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: It bears on the 1:16/1:17 seam, which no mark supports; medium is right and the end review may wish to see it.
